subject: A four-year study tied smoking and hypertension to white matter damage
script: From Agewell Brief: A four-year study tied smoking and hypertension to white matter damage. A four-year Lund University study shows smoking, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease accelerate white matter damage, a key driver of vascular dementia. The findings suggest that addressing these risks could delay cognitive decline by reducing multiple brain insults simultaneously. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
